The latter argument is strengthened by Corollary 2, and the proof is complete.

B.13 Vector and Matrix Bernstein Inequalities

For completeness, we restate Kohler and Lucchi (2017, Lemma 18), incorporating corrections for minor typographical errors. Lemma 19 is utilized by Lemma 5. Next, Lemma 20 is introduced and utilized by Lemma 22, which in turn is utilized by Lemma 6. Lemma 21 is also used by Lemma 22.

Lemma 19 (Vector Bernstein Inequality).

Let 𝐱1,𝐱2,…​𝐱n\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2},\dots\mathbf{x}_{n} be independent random vectors of common dimension dd and assume that each one is centered, uniformly bounded, and also the variance is bounded from above, i.e.,

𝔼⁡[𝐱i]=𝟎​ and ​‖𝐱i‖2≤ϑ​ as well as ​𝔼​[‖𝐱i‖22]≤σ2.\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{i}]=\mathbf{0}\text{ and }\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{i}\right\rVert_{2}\leq\vartheta\text{ as well as }\mathbb{E}[\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{i}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}]\leq\sigma^{2}. (227)

Let 𝐳=1n​∑i=1n𝐱i\mathbf{z}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf{x}_{i}. Then we have

Pr⁡(‖𝐳‖2≥ϵ)≤exp⁡(−n​ϵ28​σ2+14),\Pr(\left\lVert\mathbf{z}\right\rVert_{2}\geq\epsilon)\leq\exp\left(-n\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{8\sigma^{2}}+\frac{1}{4}\right), (228)

with 0<ϵ<σ2/ϑ+σ0<\epsilon<\sigma^{2}/\vartheta+\sigma.

Proof.

A proof can be found in (Kohler and Lucchi, 2017, Lemma 18). However, some typographical errors were identified, leading us to reproduce the proof for clarity.

The Vector Bernstein inequality for independent, zero-mean random vectors  Gross (2011, Theorem 12) states

Pr⁡(1n​‖∑i=1n𝐱i‖2≥1n​(t+V))≤exp⁡(−t24​V),\Pr\left(\frac{1}{n}\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf{x}_{i}\right\rVert_{2}\geq\frac{1}{n}(t+\sqrt{V})\right)\leq\exp\left(-\frac{t^{2}}{4V}\right), (229)

where V=∑i=1n𝔼⁡[‖𝐱i‖22]V=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{i}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}] is the sum of the traces of the covariance matrices of the centered vectors 𝐱i\mathbf{x}_{i}. Using 𝔼⁡[‖𝐱i‖22]≤σ2\mathbb{E}[\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{i}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}]\leq\sigma^{2} yields V≤n​σ2V\leq n\sigma^{2}.

Note that in (229), the probability condition is scaled by a factor of 1/n1/n to align with the subsequent analysis involving 𝐳\mathbf{z}. Let ϵ=(t+V)/n⇔t=n​ϵ−V\epsilon=(t+\sqrt{V})/n\Leftrightarrow t=n\epsilon-\sqrt{V}. Using (229) we get

Pr⁡(‖𝐳‖2≥ϵ)≤exp⁡(−14​(n​ϵ−VV)2)=exp⁡(−14​(n​ϵV−1)2).\Pr\left(\left\lVert\mathbf{z}\right\rVert_{2}\geq\epsilon\right)\leq\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{n\epsilon-\sqrt{V}}{\sqrt{V}}\right)^{2}\right)=\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{n\epsilon}{\sqrt{V}}-1\right)^{2}\right). (230)

We claim that

−14​(n​ϵV−1)2≤−14​n2​ϵ22​V+14\displaystyle-\frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{n\epsilon}{\sqrt{V}}-1\right)^{2}\leq-\frac{1}{4}\frac{n^{2}\epsilon^{2}}{2V}+\frac{1}{4} (231)

Indeed, if (231) holds we arrive at a valid inequality

−n2​ϵ2V+2​n​ϵV−1≤−12​n2​ϵ2V+1\displaystyle-\frac{n^{2}\epsilon^{2}}{V}+2\frac{n\epsilon}{\sqrt{V}}-1\leq-\frac{1}{2}\frac{n^{2}\epsilon^{2}}{V}+1 (232)
⇔\displaystyle\Leftrightarrow (n​ϵ2​V−2)2≥0.\displaystyle\left(\frac{n\epsilon}{\sqrt{2V}}-\sqrt{2}\right)^{2}\geq 0.

Using (231) in (230) gives

Pr⁡(‖𝐳‖2≥ϵ)≤exp⁡(−n​ϵ28​σ2+14),\Pr\left(\left\lVert\mathbf{z}\right\rVert_{2}\geq\epsilon\right)\leq\exp\left(-n\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{8\sigma^{2}}+\frac{1}{4}\right), (233)

where V≤n​σ2V\leq n\sigma^{2} is used. According to Gross (2011, Theorem 12), t<V/maxi⁡‖𝐱i‖2t<V/\max_{i}\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{i}\right\rVert_{2}. For V≤n​σ2V\leq n\sigma^{2} and ‖𝐱i‖2≤ϑ\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{i}\right\rVert_{2}\leq\vartheta gives t<n​σ2/ϑt<n\sigma^{2}/\vartheta. Given V≤n​σ2V\leq n\sigma^{2} and t<n​σ2/ϑt<n\sigma^{2}/\vartheta, we arrive at

n​ϵ=t+V≤n​σ2ϑ+n​σ⇔ϵ≤σ2ϑ+σ,n\epsilon=t+\sqrt{V}\leq\frac{n\sigma^{2}}{\vartheta}+\sqrt{n}\sigma\Leftrightarrow\epsilon\leq\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\vartheta}+\sigma, (234)

where x<x\sqrt{x}<x with x>1x>1 is used. In addition, it can be shown that Var⁡(𝐳)≤σ2/n\mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{z})\leq\sigma^{2}/n Gross (2011, Theorem 12) establishing (228), which concluded the proof. ∎

Lemma 20.

Let 𝐮i:Ω𝐮i→ℝn\mathbf{u}_{i}:\Omega_{\mathbf{u}_{i}}\to\mathbb{R}^{n} and 𝐯j:Ω𝐯j→ℝm\mathbf{v}_{j}:\Omega_{\mathbf{v}_{j}}\to\mathbb{R}^{m} be independent random vectors for each i,ji,j. Let g:ℝn×ℝm→ℝd×dg:\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}^{m}\to\mathbb{R}^{d\times d} be a function that produces random matrices. Then, for any indices (i,j)≠(k,l)(i,j)\neq(k,l), the matrices g⁡(𝐮i,𝐯j)g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j}) and g⁡(𝐮k,𝐯l)g(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l}) are independent, regardless of whether 𝐮i\mathbf{u}_{i} and 𝐯j\mathbf{v}_{j} come from the same or different distributions.

Proof.

Let two threshold matrices 𝐌\mathbf{M} and 𝐌′\mathbf{M}^{\prime} (which are symmetric d×dd\times d matrices), and consider the probability

P⁡(g⁡(𝐮i,𝐯j) ⋖− 𝐌∩g⁡(𝐮k,𝐯l) ⋖− 𝐌′),P(g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}\cap g(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}^{\prime}), (235)

using the element-wise comparison operator  ⋖− \mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}. Given that 𝐮i:Ω𝐮i→ℝn\mathbf{u}_{i}:\Omega_{\mathbf{u}_{i}}\to\mathbb{R}^{n} and 𝐯j:Ω𝐯j→ℝm\mathbf{v}_{j}:\Omega_{\mathbf{v}_{j}}\to\mathbb{R}^{m} are independent random vectors, and g:ℝn×ℝm→ℝd×dg:\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}^{m}\to\mathbb{R}^{d\times d} is a function generating random matrices, we rewrite the event as

{g(𝐮i,𝐯j) ⋖− 𝐌}≡{(ω𝐮i,ω𝐯j)∈Ω𝐮i×Ω𝐯j:g(𝐮i(ω𝐮i),𝐯j(ω𝐯j)) ⋖− 𝐌}≡{(𝐮i,𝐯j)∈ℝn×ℝm:g⁡(𝐮i,𝐯j) ⋖− 𝐌}.\{g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}\}\equiv\{(\omega_{\mathbf{u}_{i}},\omega_{\mathbf{v}_{j}})\in\Omega_{\mathbf{u}_{i}}\times\Omega_{\mathbf{v}_{j}}:g(\mathbf{u}_{i}(\omega_{\mathbf{u}_{i}}),\mathbf{v}_{j}(\omega_{\mathbf{v}_{j}}))\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}\}\\ \equiv\{(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}^{m}:g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}\}. (236)

Similarly, we have

{g(𝐮k,𝐯l) ⋖− 𝐌′}≡{(ω𝐮k,ω𝐯l)∈Ω𝐮k×Ω𝐯l:g(𝐮k(ω𝐮k),𝐯l(ω𝐯l)) ⋖− 𝐌′}≡{(𝐮k,𝐯l)∈ℝn×ℝm:g⁡(𝐮k,𝐯l) ⋖− 𝐌′}.\{g(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}^{\prime}\}\equiv\{(\omega_{\mathbf{u}_{k}},\omega_{\mathbf{v}_{l}})\in\Omega_{\mathbf{u}_{k}}\times\Omega_{\mathbf{v}_{l}}:g(\mathbf{u}_{k}(\omega_{\mathbf{u}_{k}}),\mathbf{v}_{l}(\omega_{\mathbf{v}_{l}}))\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}^{\prime}\}\\ \equiv\{(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}^{m}:g(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}^{\prime}\}. (237)

Let

A={(𝐮i,𝐯j)∈ℝn×ℝm:g⁡(𝐮i,𝐯j) ⋖− 𝐌}A=\{(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}^{m}:g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}\} (238)

and

B={(𝐮k,𝐯l)∈ℝn×ℝm:g⁡(𝐮k,𝐯l) ⋖− 𝐌′}.B=\{(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}^{m}:g(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}^{\prime}\}. (239)

Then using (236) and (237) in (235), we write

P({g(𝐮i,𝐯j) ⋖− 𝐌}∩{g(𝐮k,𝐯l) ⋖− 𝐌′})=P((𝐮i,𝐯j)∈A∩(𝐮k,𝐯l)∈B).P(\{g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}\}\cap\{g(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}^{\prime}\})=P((\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\in A\cap(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\in B). (240)

Recall that the sequences {𝐮i}\{\mathbf{u}_{i}\} and {𝐯j}\{\mathbf{v}_{j}\} are independent families of random variables which implies that the pairs (𝐮i,𝐯j)(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j}) are formed by drawing independently from these families. Thus, since 𝐮i\mathbf{u}_{i} and 𝐯j\mathbf{v}_{j} are independent for each (i,j)(i,j), and (𝐮k,𝐯l)(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l}) are also independent, we have

P({g(𝐮i,𝐯j) ⋖− 𝐌}∩{g(𝐮k,𝐯l) ⋖− 𝐌′})=P((𝐮i,𝐯j)∈A)P((𝐮k,𝐯l)∈B),P(\{g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}\}\cap\{g(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}^{\prime}\})=P((\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\in A)P((\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\in B), (241)

which implies

P({g(𝐮i,𝐯j) ⋖− 𝐌}∩{g(𝐮k,𝐯l) ⋖− 𝐌′})=P(g(𝐮i,𝐯j) ⋖− 𝐌)P(g(𝐮k,𝐯l) ⋖− 𝐌′),P(\{g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}\}\cap\{g(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}^{\prime}\})=P(g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M})P(g(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l})\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$\lessdot$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-1.66666pt\raisebox{-2.54375pt}{\hbox{$-$}}\hskip-1.66666pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathbf{M}^{\prime}), (242)

where (236) and (237) are used. Since the joint probability factorizes, this proves that g⁡(𝐮i,𝐯j)g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j}) and g⁡(𝐮k,𝐯l)g(\mathbf{u}_{k},\mathbf{v}_{l}) are independent whenever (i,j)≠(k,l)(i,j)\neq(k,l), regardless of whether 𝐮i\mathbf{u}_{i} and 𝐯j\mathbf{v}_{j} come from the same or different distributions. ∎

Lemma 21.

Let 𝐗∈ℝd×d\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d} be a symmetric mean-zero matrix with ‖𝐗‖≤1\left\lVert\mathbf{X}\right\rVert\leq 1 almost surely. Then,

𝔼⁡[exp⁡(λ​𝐗)]⪯exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​𝔼​[𝐗2]),\mathbb{E}\left[\exp(\lambda\mathbf{X})\right]\preceq\exp\left(g(\lambda)\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}^{2}]\right), (243)

where g⁡(λ)=eλ−λ−1g(\lambda)=e^{\lambda}-\lambda-1.

Proof.

We refer the reader to (Vershynin, 2018). ∎

Lemma 22 (Matrix Bernstein Inequality).

Let 𝐗i​j=Δg⁡(𝐮i,𝐯j)\mathbf{X}_{ij}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\Delta}}{{=}}g(\mathbf{u}_{i},\mathbf{v}_{j}) be d×dd\times d zero-mean random matrices with two independent sources of randomness, 𝐮i\mathbf{u}_{i} and 𝐯j\mathbf{v}_{j}. Also, let {𝐗i​j}i,j=1N,M\{\mathbf{X}_{ij}\}_{i,j=1}^{N,M} be a set of independent random matrices of common dimension d×dd\times d, such that ‖𝐗i​j‖2≤K\left\lVert\mathbf{X}_{ij}\right\rVert_{2}\leq K almost surely for all i,ji,j. Then, for every t≥0t\geq 0, we have

Pr⁡(‖∑i=1N∑j=1M𝐗i​j‖2≥t)≤2​d​exp⁡(−t2/2σ2+K​t/3).\Pr\left(\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathbf{X}_{ij}\right\rVert_{2}\geq t\right)\leq 2d\exp\left(-\frac{t^{2}/2}{\sigma^{2}+Kt/3}\right). (244)

Here, the matrix variance is given by

σ2=‖∑i=1N∑j=1M𝔼⁡[𝐗i​j2]‖2.\sigma^{2}=\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbf{X}_{ij}^{2}\right]\right\rVert_{2}. (245)

In particular, we can express this bound as a mixture of sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential tails, just like in the scalar Bernstein’s inequality:

Pr⁡(‖∑i=1N∑j=1M𝐗i​j‖2≥t)≤2​d​exp⁡(−38​min⁡{t2σ2,tK}).\Pr\left(\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathbf{X}_{ij}\right\rVert_{2}\geq t\right)\leq 2d\exp\left(-\frac{3}{8}\min\left\{\frac{t^{2}}{\sigma^{2}},\frac{t}{K}\right\}\right). (246)
Proof.

The following analysis is based on (Vershynin, 2018, Theorem 5.4.1).

Reduction of MGF. To bound the norm of the sum

𝐒=Δ∑i=1N∑j=1M𝐗i​j,\mathbf{S}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\Delta}}{{=}}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathbf{X}_{ij}, (247)

we need to control the largest and smallest eigenvalues of 𝐒\mathbf{S}. We can do this separately. To put this formally, consider the largest eigenvalue

λmax​(𝐒)=Δmaxi⁡λi​(𝐒)\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\Delta}}{{=}}\max_{i}\lambda_{i}(\mathbf{S}) (248)

and note that

‖𝐒‖2=max⁡|λi​(𝐒)|=max⁡{λmax​(𝐒),λmax​(−𝐒)}\left\lVert\mathbf{S}\right\rVert_{2}=\max|\lambda_{i}(\mathbf{S})|=\max\{\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S}),\lambda_{\max}(-\mathbf{S})\} (249)

and

Pr⁡(|λmax​(𝐒)|≥t)=Pr⁡(λmax​(𝐒)≥t)+Pr⁡(λmax​(−𝐒)≥t)−Pr⁡(λmax​(𝐒)≥t​ and ​λmax​(−𝐒)≥t),\Pr(|\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})|\geq t)=\Pr(\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})\geq t)+\Pr(\lambda_{\max}(-\mathbf{S})\geq t)-\Pr(\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})\geq t\text{ and }\lambda_{\max}(-\mathbf{S})\geq t), (250)

which implies

Pr⁡(|λmax​(𝐒)|≥t)≤Pr⁡(λmax​(𝐒)≥t)+Pr⁡(λmax​(−𝐒)≥t).\Pr(|\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})|\geq t)\leq\Pr(\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})\geq t)+\Pr(\lambda_{\max}(-\mathbf{S})\geq t). (251)

To bound λmax​(𝐒)\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S}), we proceed with computing the moment generating function. We fix λ≥0\lambda\geq 0 and use Markov’s inequality to obtain

Pr⁡(λmax​(𝐒)≥t)=Pr⁡(eλ​λmax​(𝐒)≥eλ​t)≤e−λ​t​𝔼​[eλ​λmax​(𝐒)].\Pr(\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})\geq t)=\Pr(e^{\lambda\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})}\geq e^{\lambda t})\leq e^{-\lambda t}\>\mathbb{E}[e^{\lambda\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})}]. (252)

Since by Vershynin (2018, Definition 5.4.2) the eigenvalues of eλ​𝐒e^{\lambda\mathbf{S}} are eλ​λi​(𝐒)e^{\lambda\lambda_{i}(\mathbf{S})}, we have

E=Δ𝔼⁡[eλ​λmax​(𝐒)]=𝔼⁡[λmax​(eλ​𝐒)].{E}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\Delta}}{{=}}\mathbb{E}[e^{\lambda\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})}]=\mathbb{E}[\lambda_{\max}(e^{\lambda\mathbf{S}})]. (253)

Since the eigenvalues of eλ​𝐒e^{\lambda\mathbf{S}} are all positive, the maximum eigenvalue of eλ​𝐒e^{\lambda\mathbf{S}} is bounded by the sum of all eigenvalues, the trace of eλ​𝐒e^{\lambda\mathbf{S}}, which leads to

E≤𝔼⁡[Tr⁡(eλ​𝐒)].{E}\leq\mathbb{E}[\Tr(e^{\lambda\mathbf{S}})]. (254)

Application of Lieb’s inequality. First note that

𝐒=∑i=1N−1∑j=1M−1𝐗i​j+∑i=1N−1𝐗i​M+∑j=1M−1𝐗N​j+𝐗N​M.\mathbf{S}=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\mathbf{X}_{ij}+\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathbf{X}_{iM}+\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\mathbf{X}_{Nj}+\mathbf{X}_{NM}. (255)

To prepare the application of Lieb’s inequality in Vershynin (2018, Lemma 5.4.9), let us separate the last term from the sum 𝐒\mathbf{S}

E[≤𝔼Tr(exp(∑i=1N−1∑j=1M−1λ𝐗i​j+∑i=1N−1λ𝐗i​M+∑j=1M−1λ𝐗N​j+λ𝐗N​M))].{E}\Biggl[\leq\mathbb{E}\,\Tr\Biggl(\exp\Biggl(\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}+\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{iM}+\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{Nj}+\lambda\mathbf{X}_{NM}\Biggr)\Biggr)\Biggr]. (256)

Conditioning on {𝐗i​j}i,j=1N−1,M−1\{\mathbf{X}_{ij}\}_{i,j=1}^{N-1,M-1} and applying Vershynin (2018, Lemma 5.4.9) for the fixed matrix

𝐇=Δ∑i=1N−1∑j=1M−1λ​𝐗i​j+∑i=1N−1λ​𝐗i​M+∑j=1M−1λ​𝐗N​j\mathbf{H}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\Delta}}{{=}}\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}+\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{iM}+\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{Nj} (257)

and the random matrix 𝐙=Δλ​𝐗N​M\mathbf{Z}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\Delta}}{{=}}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{NM}, we obtain

E≤𝔼{𝐗i​j}i,j=1N,M​[Tr⁡(exp⁡(∑i=1N−1∑j=1M−1λ​𝐗i​j+∑i=1N−1λ​𝐗i​M+∑j=1M−1λ​𝐗N​j+λ​𝐗N​M))]≤𝔼{𝐗i​j}i,j=1N−1,M−1​[𝔼𝐗N​M​[Tr⁡(exp⁡(∑i=1N−1∑j=1M−1λ​𝐗i​j+∑i=1N−1λ​𝐗i​M+∑j=1M−1λ​𝐗N​j+λ​𝐗N​M))]]≤𝔼{𝐗i​j}i,j=1N−1,M−1​[Tr⁡(exp⁡(∑i=1N−1∑j=1M−1λ​𝐗i​j+∑i=1N−1λ​𝐗i​M+∑j=1M−1λ​𝐗N​j+log⁡𝔼𝐗N​M​eλ​𝐗N​M))].{E}\leq\mathbb{E}_{\{\mathbf{X}_{ij}\}_{i,j=1}^{N,M}}\Biggl[\Tr\Biggl(\exp\Biggl(\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}+\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{iM}+\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{Nj}+\lambda\mathbf{X}_{NM}\Biggr)\Biggr)\Biggr]\\ \leq\mathbb{E}_{\{\mathbf{X}_{ij}\}_{i,j=1}^{N-1,M-1}}\Biggl[\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{X}_{NM}}\Biggl[\Tr\Biggl(\exp\Biggl(\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}+\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{iM}+\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{Nj}+\lambda\mathbf{X}_{NM}\Biggr)\Biggr)\Biggr]\Biggr]\\ \leq\mathbb{E}_{\{\mathbf{X}_{ij}\}_{i,j=1}^{N-1,M-1}}\Biggl[\Tr\Biggl(\exp\Biggl(\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}+\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{iM}+\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\lambda\mathbf{X}_{Nj}+\log\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{X}_{NM}}e^{\lambda\mathbf{X}_{NM}}\Biggr)\Biggr)\Biggr]. (258)

We continue similarly: separate the next term λ​𝐗N−1,M−1\lambda\mathbf{X}_{N-1,M-1} from the remaining sum and apply Vershynin (2018, Lemma 5.4.9) again for 𝐙=λ​𝐗N−1,M−1\mathbf{Z}=\lambda\mathbf{X}_{N-1,M-1}. Repeating this process N​MNM times, we obtain

Pr⁡(λmax​(𝐒)≥t)≤Tr⁡(e−λ​t​exp⁡(∑i=1N∑j=1Mlog⁡𝔼​exp⁡λ​𝐗i​j)).\Pr(\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})\geq t)\leq\Tr\left(e^{-\lambda t}\exp\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{M}\log\mathbb{E}\,\exp{\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}}\right)\right). (259)

MGF of the individual terms. It remains to bound the matrix-valued moment generating function 𝔼​eλ​𝐗i​j\mathbb{E}\,e^{\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}} for each term 𝐗i​j\mathbf{X}_{ij}. We now use Lemma 21.

Completion of the proof. Using Lemma 21, we obtain

𝔼⁡[exp⁡(λ​𝐗i​j/K)]⪯exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​𝔼​[𝐗i​j2]/K2)⇔∏i,j=1N,M𝔼⁡[exp⁡(λ​𝐗i​j/K)]⪯∏i,j=1N,Mexp⁡(g⁡(λ)​𝔼​[𝐗i​j2]/K2)⇔∏i,j=1N,M𝔼⁡[exp⁡(λ​𝐗i​j/K)]⪯exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​∑i,j=1N,M𝔼⁡[𝐗i​j2]/K2),\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}/K\right)\right]\preceq\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}_{ij}^{2}]/K^{2}\right)\Leftrightarrow\prod_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}/K\right)\right]\preceq\prod_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}_{ij}^{2}]/K^{2}\right)\\ \Leftrightarrow\prod_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}/K\right)\right]\preceq\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\sum_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}_{ij}^{2}]/K^{2}\right), (260)

which implies

∏i,j=1N,M𝔼⁡[exp⁡(λ​𝐗i​j/K)]⪯exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​∑i,j=1N,M𝔼⁡[𝐗i​j2]/K2).\prod_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}/K\right)\right]\preceq\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\sum_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}_{ij}^{2}]/K^{2}\right). (261)

Also, given that 𝐗i​j\mathbf{X}_{ij} are independent, we have

∏i,j=1N,M𝔼⁡[exp⁡(λ​𝐗i​j/K)]=exp⁡(log⁡(∏i,j=1N,M𝔼​exp⁡(λ​𝐗i​j/K)))=exp⁡(∑i,j=1N,Mlog⁡𝔼​exp⁡(λ​𝐗i​j/K)),\prod_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}/K\right)\right]=\exp\left(\log\left(\prod_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\mathbb{E}\exp\left(\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}/K\right)\right)\right)=\\ \exp\left(\sum_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\log\mathbb{E}\exp\left(\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}/K\right)\right), (262)

which combined with (261)

exp⁡(∑i,j=1N,Mlog⁡𝔼​exp⁡(λ​𝐗i​j/K))⪯exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​∑i,j=1N,M𝔼⁡[𝐗i​j2]/K2),\exp\left(\sum_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\log\mathbb{E}\exp\left(\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}/K\right)\right)\preceq\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\sum_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}_{ij}^{2}]/K^{2}\right), (263)

and applying the trace to both sides yields

Tr⁡(exp⁡(∑i,j=1N,Mlog⁡𝔼​exp⁡(λ​𝐗i​j/K)))≤Tr⁡(exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​𝐙~/K2)),\Tr\left(\exp\left(\sum_{i,j=1}^{N,M}\log\mathbb{E}\exp\left(\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}/K\right)\right)\right)\leq\Tr\left(\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}/K^{2}\right)\right), (264)

where 𝐙~=Δ𝔼⁡[∑i=1N∑j=1M𝐗i​j2]\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\Delta}}{{=}}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathbf{X}_{ij}^{2}\right]. Since the trace of exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​𝐙~/K2)\exp(g(\lambda)\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}/K^{2}) is a sum of dd positive eigenvalues, it is bounded by dd times the maximum eigenvalue and using Vershynin (2018, Definition 5.4.2), we obtain

Tr⁡(exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​𝐙~/K2))≤d​λmax​(exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​𝐙~/K2))=d​exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​λmax​(𝐙~/K2))=d​exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​‖𝐙~‖/K2)=d​exp⁡(g⁡(λ)​σ2/K2).\Tr\left(\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}/K^{2}\right)\right)\leq d\>\lambda_{\max}\left(\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}/K^{2}\right)\right)=d\>\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\lambda_{\max}(\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}/K^{2})\right)\\ =d\>\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\|\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}\|/K^{2}\right)=d\>\exp\left(g(\lambda)\>\sigma^{2}/K^{2}\right). (265)

Combining (259) and (265) we get

Pr⁡(λmax​(𝐒)≥K​t)≤e−λ​t​Tr⁡(exp⁡(∑i=1N∑j=1Mlog⁡𝔼​exp​λ​𝐗i​j/K))≤d​exp⁡(−λ​t+g⁡(λ)​σ2/K2),\Pr(\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})\geq Kt)\leq e^{-\lambda t}\Tr\left(\exp\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{M}\log\mathbb{E}\,\exp{\lambda\mathbf{X}_{ij}/K}\right)\right)\leq d\>\exp\left(-\lambda t+g(\lambda)\>\sigma^{2}/K^{2}\right), (266)

which implies

Pr⁡(λmax​(𝐒)≥t)≤d​exp⁡(−λK​t+g⁡(λ)K2​σ2).\Pr(\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})\geq t)\leq d\>\exp\left(-\frac{\lambda}{K}t+\frac{g(\lambda)}{K^{2}}\sigma^{2}\right). (267)

Minimizing over λ>0\lambda>0, the minimum occurs at

λ=log⁡(1+K​tσ2),t≥0.\lambda=\log\left(1+\frac{Kt}{\sigma^{2}}\right),\quad t\geq 0. (268)

Plugging this into the bound, we get

Pr⁡(λmax​(𝐒)≥t)≤d​exp⁡(−σ2K2​h​(K​tσ2)),\Pr\left(\lambda_{\max}\left(\mathbf{S}\right)\geq t\right)\leq d\>\exp\left(-\frac{\sigma^{2}}{K^{2}}\>h\left(\frac{Kt}{\sigma^{2}}\right)\right), (269)

where

h⁡(u)=(1+u)​log⁡(1+u)−u,for ​u>0.h(u)=(1+u)\log(1+u)-u,\quad\text{for }u>0. (270)

We know that Boucheron et al. (2013, Exercise 2.8)

h⁡(u)≥u22​(1+u/3),h(u)\geq\frac{u^{2}}{2(1+u/3)}, (271)

with u>0u>0 and thus

Pr⁡(λmax​(𝐒)≥t)≤d​exp⁡(−σ2K2​u22​(1+u/3)),\Pr\left(\lambda_{\max}\left(\mathbf{S}\right)\geq t\right)\leq d\>\exp\left(-\frac{\sigma^{2}}{K^{2}}\>\frac{u^{2}}{2(1+u/3)}\right), (272)

where u=K​tσ2u=\frac{Kt}{\sigma^{2}}. Substituting uu in (272), we obtain

Pr⁡(λmax​(𝐒)≥t)≤d​exp⁡(−t2/2σ2+K​t/3).\Pr\left(\lambda_{\max}\left(\mathbf{S}\right)\geq t\right)\leq d\>\exp\left(-\frac{t^{2}/2}{\sigma^{2}+Kt/3}\right). (273)

Following similar steps with −𝐒-\mathbf{S} instead of 𝐒\mathbf{S} and using (251), yields

P⁡(|λmax​(𝐒)|≥t)≤{2​d​exp⁡(−3​t28​σ2),t≤σ2/K2​d​exp⁡(−3​t8​K),t>σ2/K.P(|\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})|\geq t)\leq\begin{cases}2d\exp\left(\frac{-3t^{2}}{8\sigma^{2}}\right),\quad t\leq\sigma^{2}/K\\ 2d\exp\left(\frac{-3t}{8K}\right),\quad t>\sigma^{2}/K.\end{cases} (274)

Intuitively, for small tt, i.e., t≤σ2/Kt\leq\sigma^{2}/K, we have a sub-Gaussian bound, while for large tt, i.e., t>σ2/Kt>\sigma^{2}/K, we have a sub-exponential bound. Looking for the tightest bound, we may write

P⁡(|λmax​(𝐒)|≥t)≤2​d​exp⁡(−38​min⁡{t2σ2,tK}).P(|\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S})|\geq t)\leq 2d\exp\left(-\frac{3}{8}\min\left\{\frac{t^{2}}{\sigma^{2}},\frac{t}{K}\right\}\right). (275)
